name: McLeod Ganj
tagline: Tibetan hub and Dalai Lama's home
description: The main upper town and seat of the Tibetan government in exile, home to the Dalai Lama's temple. It buzzes with cafes, monasteries, shops and travellers, offering the widest choice of food, guesthouses and services in the area.
bestFor: Travellers wanting cafes, culture, meetups and the most amenities

name: Bhagsu
description: A short walk from McLeod Ganj, Bhagsu is known for its waterfall, ancient temple and a laid-back cafe scene popular with long-stay travellers. It offers cheaper rooms than McLeod while staying close to its shops and restaurants.
bestFor: Budget long-stayers wanting cafes and quiet near McLeod Ganj

name: Dharamkot
description: A tranquil forested village above McLeod Ganj, popular with yoga practitioners, meditators and long-stay nomads. It has quiet guesthouses, small cafes and forest trails including the route to Triund, with calmer, greener surroundings.
bestFor: Nomads seeking quiet, nature, yoga and long slow stays

name: Lower Dharamshala
tagline: Local town with transport and services
description: The lower main town holds the bus stand, markets, banks and government offices, with a more everyday Indian feel than the upper villages. It is cheaper and better connected but lacks the traveller cafes and views of McLeod Ganj above.
bestFor: Those prioritising cheap rent, transport and everyday local services
